args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP while tests/test_money.py (and
the docstring) expect banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), causing
the nightly build failure. Switch the rounding mode to make the
half-even cases (e.g. 2.665 -> 2.66) behave correctly.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-round-half-even
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP` — despite its docstring already claiming banker's rounding.

## Changes

- `src/money.py`: switched the quantize rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

This makes the half-even cases behave correctly, e.g. `Decimal("2.665")` now rounds to `2.66` instead of `2.67`.

## Testing

- CI run [ci-0001] on this branch passed (all tests green).

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Diagnosis:** `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `round_money()` even though FIN-212 (and its own docstring) require banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`), which is what `tests/test_money.py` asserts — causing the nightly build failure.
- **Fix:** Created branch `fix/FIN-212-round-half-even` and changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (e.g., `2.665` now correctly rounds to `2.66`).
- **CI:** Ran CI on the branch (run `ci-0001`) — all tests passed.
- **PR:** Opened PR #101 against main requesting review from alex: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I did not merge it, since merging into main requires code-owner approval per policy.

transcript.reasoning_content: Let me look at the files first.

transcript.content: The bug is clear: the docstring mentions banker's rounding, but the implementation uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` instead of `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Let me fix it on a new branch.
transcript.reasoning_content: The docstring says HALF_EVEN but impl is HALF_UP. Fix: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN. 2.675 → 2.68 (half-even: 3rd digit... 2.675 quantized to 0.01: last kept digit 7, remainder 5, round to even → 2.68? 7 is odd, round half even goes to 8. Yes 2.68). 2.665 → 2.66 (6 is even). Correct.
